Task-Obsession: find-or-create, land digests, overlap signals, merge gates

Wish. Every change in Barkpark flows through a task — when work arrives, we find the matching task (or create one and expand it), we never land the same change twice, and changes that negatively interact are never hidden inside separate tasks. Enforcement lives in write verbs and CI, never in agent discipline.

Grounding (what exists today)

  • The close "work-digest fence" guards brief drift only (title/description/criteria changed under claim → 409). It records nothing about what code landed.
  • Full-text search exists (doc.search, postgres/indx engines). There is no match/dedup/overlap capability in the manifest.
  • Rail notices (rail_changed, advisory-never-gate) are the delivery channel for in-flight signals.
  • Dependencies are task_edges rows: POST /v1/tasks/edges {from_id, to_id, kind:"blocks"}. The dependencies content field is a dead key.

Design — four layers

1. Find-or-create at intake (the check lives inside task.create)

task.create runs similarity against open and recently-closed tasks server-side. Above threshold it refuses, returning similar:[…], and requires --distinct-from <id> (an explicit "I saw it, this is different") or steers to claim/expand the existing task via parent_id. Closed candidates catch the land-the-same-change-twice case before any work starts. Two tiers:

  • Tier 1 — mechanical, always on, dependency-free: Postgres FTS + label/capability overlap. Core Barkpark works with no API key (plugins-off doctrine).
  • Tier 2 — LLM judge, env-gated: gray-zone pairs go to claude-opus-4-8 with structured outputs (output_config.format json_schema) returning {relation: duplicate|expands|already_landed|distinct, confidence, reason}. Judging rubric before the cache breakpoint, the two briefs after it (burst creates read the cached prefix). Fail open to tier 1 when no key is configured or the call errors — the gate never blocks on Anthropic availability.

2. Land digest at close (record what changed, not just that it closed)

Close writes landed: {prs, files, capability_slugs} — auto-derivable from the PR diff; slugs from the @canonical vocabulary. Closed tasks become a queryable ledger of what surface each change touched. Task↔PR is many-to-many (one PR closes several concerns; one task spans several PRs) — the digest is a list, never a scalar.

3. Scope stamping + overlap notices in flight

Claim stamps the task with predicted scope (files + capability slugs — the local scope tooling computes exactly this). Server-side, two comparisons, both advisory on the existing rail-notice channel: live-claim scopes pairwise (scope_overlap to both workers) and every fresh land digest against live scopes (landed_under_you: "task X landed changes in files you're scoped to — rebase before continuing"). Hot files (manifest, router card, test helpers) are weighted down so the signal doesn't saturate.

4. Merge gates in CI (the hard line)

  • PR↔task gate: every PR must reference a task that is claimed by the author and in progress — no task, no merge (same shape as the changeset gate). Merge-base cutoff so pre-existing open PRs don't red on rollout.
  • Re-land check: PR files vs land digests of recently-closed tasks; high overlap with no dependency edge → advisory warning on the PR (mechanical file overlap; an LLM verdict may annotate but never hard-blocks a merge).

Ratified decisions (the four load-bearing footguns)

  1. D1 — Friction that can't become ritual. --distinct-from must name a real candidate from the rejection; rejections are logged on the task doc; a periodic audit reviews the rejection trail. Scripted epic seeding uses a sanctioned --sibling-of <epic> so waves don't learn to bypass.
  2. D2 — Silence is never clearance. Scope re-stamps on every lease renewal (the existing heartbeat verb); every notice carries an "as of" timestamp so staleness is visible. Stated contract: absence of an overlap notice is not proof of no conflict.
  3. D3 — The emergency lane satisfies the invariant instead of skipping it. The PR↔task gate never blocks a hotfix: a hotfix! label auto-files the task. The gate is required-by-name in branch protection so a silently-skipped check (conflicted PR) cannot read as green.
  4. D4 — One ledger of record. The repo declares its task ledger (guerrilla) in config. Matcher, digest, and overlap run server-side on that instance only; local bp instances are dev sandboxes with no dedup guarantee.

Footgun register (the other ten, for builders)

  • Textual matcher is semantically blind both ways (Cody dup-audit precedent) — hence tier 2, calibrated before it gates anything.
  • "Recently closed" window: too short misses re-lands, too long blocks legitimate re-attempts; closed ≠ landed (wontfix/superseded must not block).
  • Epic seeding trips the gate by design — --sibling-of is the sanctioned path.
  • Task↔PR many-to-many — digests are lists, attribution is per-PR.
  • File paths are weak identity: renames stale the ledger; hot files saturate — weight or ignore-list, and expect that list to drift.
  • Capability slugs are deliberately sparse (@canonical is demand-driven) — files-only is the common case, not the fallback.
  • Notice fatigue poisons the shared rail channel — overlap notices must stay rarer than rail_changed or both get ignored.
  • Re-land check fires on intended overlap (reverts, follow-ups) — suppress via dependency edges; warn, never block.
  • CI silently skips on conflicted PRs — require the check by name (folded into D3).
  • Rollout reds the open-PR fleet — merge-base cutoff (folded into layer 4).

Build order

  1. CI PR↔task gate — pure CI, no schema change, makes taskless changes impossible immediately.
  2. Judge calibration batch — one-shot dedup audit of the existing open-task corpus: mechanical candidate pairs (FTS top-k, not O(n²)), gray zone through the Batch API at 50% price on claude-opus-4-8. Double duty: audits today's backlog and calibrates the tier-2 threshold against real data before it gates anything.
  3. Match-in-create (tier 1) — mechanical similarity in the create path + --distinct-from / --sibling-of + rejection trail.
  4. Tier-2 LLM judge — env-gated, structured outputs, fail-open; threshold from step 2.
  5. Land digest at close — schema addition + auto-derivation from PR diffs + CI re-land advisory.
  6. Scope stamping + overlap notices — claim-time stamp, renewal re-stamp, scope_overlap / landed_under_you rail notices.

Principle (holds across all six): every hard gate erodes via its exception path, and every advisory erodes via noise. Gates must be satisfiable under emergency (D3), advisories must stay rare enough to read (D2, hot-file weighting), and both must be tripwired (rejection audit, required-by-name checks), because agent discipline is not a mechanism.
